Reason: To turn off Wi‑Fi and enable Bluetooth, the quickest path is to open Quick Settings by pulling down from the top of the home screen.
Action: {"action_type": "scroll", "direction": "down"}

Tried to pull down Quick Settings from the home screen to access Wi‑Fi/Bluetooth, but the downward scroll instead opened the app drawer/search screen (apps list visible, status bar still shows Wi‑Fi on), so Quick Settings did not open and next step should avoid another home-screen down scroll.

Reason: We’re stuck in the app drawer/search screen. To reliably get to Wi‑Fi and Bluetooth controls, the easiest fallback is to open the Settings app directly from home rather than trying Quick Settings again from here.
Action: {"action_type": "navigate_home"}

Used navigate_home to exit the app drawer (before: launcher app list/search with many app icons; after: Nexus home screen with dock/search bar); this worked, but Wi‑Fi is still shown on in the status bar, so next open Settings from home/app list to disable Wi‑Fi and then enable Bluetooth.

Reason: Opening the Settings app directly is the easiest reliable way to turn off Wi‑Fi and enable Bluetooth, since pulling down Quick Settings did not work from the home screen.
Action: {"action_type": "open_app", "app_name": "Settings"}

Opened Settings from the home screen as intended; the screen changed to the Settings homepage showing “Network & internet” and “Connected devices,” so this worked and next should tap Network & internet to disable Wi‑Fi, then use Connected devices for Bluetooth.

Reason: To turn off Wi‑Fi first, the quickest next step is to open the Network & internet settings from the Settings homepage.
Action: {"action_type": "click", "index": 5}

Tapped **Network & internet** on the Settings homepage to reach Wi‑Fi controls; it worked and opened the **Network & internet** page showing **Internet/AndroidWifi**, so next step should be to open **Internet** to turn Wi‑Fi off.

Reason: Open the Internet settings first so I can access the Wi‑Fi toggle and turn Wi‑Fi off before enabling Bluetooth.
Action: {"action_type": "click", "index": 3}

Tapped “Internet” (index 3) intending to open Wi‑Fi controls, but the before/after screens are effectively unchanged on Network & internet, so the tap may not have registered or the screenshot didn’t update; Wi‑Fi is still on and the next step should retry opening Internet or wait/check for navigation.

Reason: The Network & internet page is still visible and Wi‑Fi is on; the previous tap on “Internet” may not have registered, so the simplest next step is to retry opening Internet to access the Wi‑Fi toggle.
Action: {"action_type": "click", "index": 3}

Tapped “Internet” (idx 3) from Network & internet intending to reach the Wi‑Fi controls, but it unexpectedly opened the “Add network” screen instead of a Wi‑Fi toggle page; Wi‑Fi still appears on, so next should back out rather than continue here.

Reason: We’re stuck in the Add network screen, which is not useful for turning off Wi‑Fi or enabling Bluetooth. The quickest recovery is to go back to the previous Settings page.
Action: {"action_type": "navigate_back"}

Went back to escape the irrelevant Add network Wi‑Fi form (SSID field, Security spinner, Cancel/Save, keyboard visible); back partly worked by dismissing the keyboard, but we are still on the same Add network screen with Wi‑Fi still on, so we should back out again to reach the main Settings/network page before toggling Wi‑Fi or Bluetooth.

Reason: We are still stuck on the Add network screen, and the visible “Navigate up” button is the clearest way to leave this page and return to Network & internet so we can turn off Wi‑Fi and then enable Bluetooth.
Action: {"action_type": "click", "index": 2}

Tapped the “Navigate up” button to exit the Add network Wi‑Fi page and get back toward settings needed for Wi‑Fi/Bluetooth, but the after screenshot only shows the status bar so the result is unclear; next verify the current screen before proceeding.

Reason: The current screen only shows the status bar/System UI, so the app content is unclear. Waiting is the safest way to let the screen render before taking the next step to continue disabling Wi‑Fi and enabling Bluetooth.
Action: {"action_type": "wait"}

Waited for the screen to render; before only the status bar was visible, and after the Settings Internet/Wi‑Fi page appeared with Wi‑Fi currently ON (switch checked), so next step should be toggling the Wi‑Fi switch off before moving to Bluetooth.

Reason: The Wi‑Fi page is open and the Wi‑Fi switch is visible and currently checked/on. To turn off Wi‑Fi, tap the switch.
Action: {"action_type": "click", "index": 11}

Tapped the Wi‑Fi switch on the Internet settings page to turn Wi‑Fi off; it worked as expected because the switch changed from checked/on to unchecked/off, the connected Wi‑Fi network list disappeared, and next step should be to enable Bluetooth.

Reason: Wi‑Fi is already off. To enable Bluetooth, the quickest path is to go back to the main Settings page and then open Connected devices/Bluetooth settings.
Action: {"action_type": "navigate_back"}

Went back from the Internet/Wi‑Fi subpage (where the Wi‑Fi switch was already off) to the broader Network & internet settings page as intended; Wi‑Fi remains off, but Bluetooth is not visible here, so next navigate toward Connected devices/Bluetooth rather than returning to Wi‑Fi.

Reason: Wi‑Fi is already off. We’re still inside Network & internet, and Bluetooth is typically under the main Settings page’s Connected devices, so the quickest next step is to go back there.
Action: {"action_type": "navigate_back"}

Navigated back from Network & internet to the main Settings page as intended; Wi‑Fi appears already off (status bar shows “Wi‑Fi will turn on automatically”/“No internet”), and now Connected devices is visible for the next step to enable Bluetooth.

Reason: Wi‑Fi is already off, and the main Settings page shows “Connected devices,” which is the simplest path to Bluetooth settings. I’ll open that section to enable Bluetooth.
Action: {"action_type": "click", "index": 7}

Tapped “Connected devices” from the main Settings screen because Wi‑Fi already appeared off; it worked and opened the Connected devices page, where Bluetooth is still off (“Bluetooth will turn on”), so the next step should be to tap a Bluetooth-related option to enable it.

Reason: On the Connected devices screen, Bluetooth is still off and the visible “Pair new device” row says “Bluetooth will turn on to pair,” which is a straightforward way to enable Bluetooth.
Action: {"action_type": "click", "index": 4}

Tapped “Pair new device” to turn on Bluetooth from Connected devices; it worked, opening the Pair new device screen with Available devices/scanning and the phone’s Bluetooth address visible, so Bluetooth is now enabled and the next step is just to finish if Wi‑Fi was already turned off.

Reason: Wi‑Fi was already turned off in step 10, and opening the “Pair new device” Bluetooth screen indicates Bluetooth has been enabled. The user’s goal is complete.
Action: {"action_type": "status", "goal_status": "complete"}
